MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 13, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:00 p.m., on July 13, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on July 8, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs

   Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under Negotiation-

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were two Closed Session Items. CS2 is regarding
property negotiations of the Stein Mart property. The City Attorney received further instruction
but no reportable action occurred. CS1 is regarding the voting right’s litigation, and the following
statement was made by Council Member Raths on behalf of the Voter Education Ad Hoc
Committee Act.

The City Council has fought to ensure that the minority voters living in Mission Viejo were
provided the greatest opportunity to have their votes have the greatest impact. After over three years
of working with two Secretaries of State, and the Governor’s Office, to best support our minority
voters, the time to make a final decision is upon us. Unlike many cities that immediately adopted
district voting, your City Council took additional community-oriented steps to see if there was a
violation and how best to cure it: (1) analyzed demographics to determine if at-large voting really
did produce voting results that violated the California Voting Right Act (it did violate the California
Voting Rights Act); and, (2) determined which voting structures being used across the nation would
give a “real” voice to minority voters rather than immediately defaulting to less beneficial district-
based voting; and (3) pursued statutory interpretations supported by the minority voters, as
plaintiffs, and the City Council, to give the best voice to the vote cost by minority voters. We have
now concluded that despite acknowledgement from the Secretary of State that change to allow
cumulative or ranked choice voting is being considered throughout the State, that continuing
Mission Viejo’s leadership in this voting issue is not helpful to Mission Viejo voters and candidates.
Sacramento has closed the door, at present, to this voting system occurring on an administrative
basis. We would need to have further litigation or a clarifying statute to offer this voting privilege
to our community. We have worked with representative of the legislature, legislative members and
two Secretaries of State. The California Voting Act allows the judicially approved options of
cumulative voting and ranked choice voting. However, these options for change are seemingly too
significant for State staff to authorize. Thus, as Sacramento will not allow ranked choice or
cumulative voting to best serve our minority residents, we must now defer to the “one size fits all”
Districts remedy. In Mission Viejo, it is not possible to form a district which includes a majority of
minority voters, because our minority voters do not live in one area; they live throughout the City.
It is unfortunate that the best interest of our minority voters cannot be served, but your City Council
tried very hard to achieve a system which would give them a greater voice. Accordingly, the Voting
Rights subcommittee comprised of the Mayor and Councilman Raths has recommended to the
whole of the City Council that, pursuant to our court order, the City proceed with the creation of
voting districts and employ them for the 2022 local election. We had sincerely hoped for a better
outcome for Mission Viejo’s minority voters, but Sacramento is not allowing any option other than
District voting. We do note and appreciate the assistance of the new California Secretary of State,
Dr. Shirley Weber, and her team, for the positive assistance they have provided to the City Council
and staff. Her insights as to possible future voting system that will better serve minority voters is
encouraging for those cities also seeking to support their minority voters.
City Council Minutes  2  July 13, 2021
 Mayor Kelley added that when the City Council meetings reconvene in August, information shall
be provided with regards to the process for district elections.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Ed Maurer, M.V.: Spoke about Community Choice Energy and ways to reduce the severity of
global warming. He asked to meet with each City Council Member to discuss CCE and how this
can be made palatable to residents of Mission Viejo. Ed suggested open forums and online
information.

Gabriel El Mahrek, M.V.: Expressed his opinion on the LGBTQ+ and outlined his thoughts.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Spoke about Brown Act violations she brought up at the last Council meeting
and that she reached out to CalAware ~ Californians Aware, and read their response. On a second
note, she encouraged voters to research SB10, which apparently gives the City Council the right to
rezone neighborhoods to allow ten unit apartment buildings.

Mr. Curley clarified that this City, and probably every City in the State is vigorously in opposition
to SB10. It does not give the City Council the authority, it gives the State the authority to impose
this on the cities. The League of California Cities ~ LOCC & other interest groups are vigorously
opposing SB10, and also SB9, SB8 & SB7. The State has taken on a very aggressive approach to
insert housing, and it is very destructive to every city residential area. He concluded by encouraging
residents to reach out and contact their legislator to oppose SB10, however, he reiterated that the
Cities and City Council are victims, and not perpetrators of this.

Sharon Cody, M.V.: Started by saying it’s great to see everyone. She gave an update on DAWG
~ Dedicated Animal Welfare Group, who have been helping animals for 26 years. Sharon
mentioned how giving the residents in Mission Viejo are, even during the Pandemic. She stated
the Shelter impounded over 1,100 pets. DAWG through various promotional events during the year,
raised $15,000 to the cause. Lastly, Sharon complemented Director Michelle Claude-Clemente on
her fabulous work at the Animal Shelter and thanked the Council for their ongoing support.

City Council Minutes  3  July 13, 2021
 Richard Walker, Public Law Center: Commented on the Orange County affordable housing and
homelessness crisis. He also voiced his concern that the City is creating a hostile environment and
discouraging public participation at City Council meetings.

Helen Maurer, M.V.: Stated climate change is upon us. We are already past the point where we
can stop climate change and need to take serious action, immediately. As a community, we need
to switch to Community Choice Energy. Helen requested the City Council begin a public discussion
of this process now, so that we can move forward.

Alex Berk, M.V.: Spoke about CCE ~ Community Choice Energy and how the City needs to act
now by reducing its carbon footprint. She asked the Council to consider CCE, and mentioned that
if they want young people to have a good life, like they had, that they need to bring CCE back on
the agenda, as soon as possible.

Walter Lawson, M.V.: Spoke on the 2022 City Council Elections. He stated that the City needs to
move to district based elections, and requested an explanation as to how the terms of the three
Council Members (Bucknum, Raths and Sachs) elected in 2018 for two-year terms were extended
in 2020 for another two years. He concluded by reiterating, that he does not feel he has received
an answer to the concerns he has with regards to their terms.

Mayor Kelley mentioned that the City Attorney had stepped away for a moment, however, she
would ask him to provide the report. She also asked Mr. Lawson to send her an email and she will
ensure that he receives a written response to his second question.

Maya Shokati, M.V.: Requested the City Council consider a 3-week long carnival event this
summer / autumn on the Village Green for Mission Viejo residents and neighboring cities to enjoy.
She stated, that with the Pandemic subsiding, residents should not have to go to other surrounding
cities to find entertainment.

Audrey Tomovich, M.V.: Voiced concerns about the environment and climate changes taking
place. She cited an article about Community Choice Aggregation, and a new electric power utility
entity, OCPA ~ Orange County Power Authority. She added that the City of Irvine conducted a
feasibility study and found substantial savings by joining CCA ~ a win-win for our City. Audrey
urged the City to have an open forum to discuss CCE.

Mayor Kelley mentioned that we heard from quite a few speakers on CCA or CCE, and shared that
OCPA is currently assisting Mission Viejo in conducting a feasibility study and we are awaiting
the results of that study. Once we receive the results, we will share them with the residents.

City Manager Dennis Wilberg added that the City has looked at this opportunity twice in the past,
and the past two efforts indicated that it would not be financially viable for the City to peruse it any
further. That being said, now that OCPA has been formed, we have met with them a couple of
times and they are doing an additional analysis. Once that information is available, staff will bring
it back to the City Council.

25. Adoption of the 2021-2023 Budget

Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson presented the staff report.

Council Member Sachs questioned the $100,000 line item pertaining to the MAC ~ Marguerite
Aquatics Center dive tower repairs.

Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay responded that unfortunately, the issues lie with the chemicals,
which are very corrosive. He explained that some of the areas on the internal part of the tower are
not draining 100% and causing some deterioration of the concrete. At the request of the dive team,
the City is trying to get ahead of this before it gets any worse, however, it entails some pretty
extensive work.

Council Member Sachs also thanked staff for going back, taking a look at the budget and reducing
it by the requested 1.3 million dollars. He knows it was not easy, and appreciates everyone who
worked on this. Mayor Kelley also thanked staff for going back over the budget.

Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve Resolution 21-
29 Adopting a Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for 2021-23 and Appropriating Funds for the
FY 2021/22 Only.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

28. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell mentioned that the Olympic Ad Hoc Committee has been meeting via
Zoom over the last year, and finally met in person for the first-time last month. It was a very
productive meeting seeing as everything has been on hold/mostly closed, but they have stayed in
touch and continued good dialogue. He stated that the next in person meeting is at Saddleback
College in the stadium, and shared the good news that Saddleback shall be reopening soon. He is
looking forward to the opportunity of promoting sports tourism again in Mission Viejo and said it
will be good to “get back on the wagon”.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths commended the City on how beautiful it is, especially driving along
Marguerite from one end to the other until you get to the eyesore called the Post Office. He stated
that a couple years ago the Rotary Club cleaned it up, however, a nonprofit group should not be
doing the work of the federal government. Council Member Raths concluded by asking the City
Manager to keep the pressure to clean up the Post Office, because apart from that, the City looks
beautiful.

City Council Minutes  10  July 13, 2021
 Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs mentioned that he had a few items to discuss prior to his proposed
Resolution. First, he stated it was great to see Sharon Cody, and suggested that maybe at the next
Council Meeting the Animal Services Department could possibly bring a dog or cat that is up for
adoption. Secondly, he thanked the residents for attending the Council meeting this evening and
discussing the Community Choice Energy, he stated that the City is and has been looking at this.
He would also like to propose, that now that the golf course is looking good, the City might want
to consider holding an annual citywide golf tournament as a fundraiser for the golf course. It would
be self-sustaining and revenue generating.

29. Long and Short-Term Post COVID-19 Policies

Council Member Sachs discussed the Resolution he is proposing for Mission Viejo to continue and
look forward to helping/sustaining our businesses.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Expressed her concerns on the proposed Policy. She stated that the City
should open a transparent process and allow business to tell us how to help them.

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1) adopt
Resolution 21-30 Establishing Long and Short-Term Post COVID-19 Policies to Preserve and
Stimulate Economic Development, Support a Balanced City Budget, and Maintain Mission Viejo's
Competitiveness in the Regions Municipal Market Place, and (2) amend Section 6 of the resolution
to include the review of the Economic Development Element by the Planning Commission.

Mayor Kelley asked that the Planning & Transportation Commission work with Staff to update the
Economic Development section of the General Plan. Council Member Sachs stated he worked with
Staff to put this together. Mayor Kelley opened this up to other Council Members for discussion
and both Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum and Council Member Goodell were in agreement of this Policy.
City Attorney Curley, suggested adding wording pertaining to Section 6.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum gave an update on SCAG ~ Southern California Association of
Governments, the So Cal Green Print Project and SB10, SB9, SB8 and SB7. She stated the next
meeting will be September 2, 2021 and will be a highbred meeting. She promoted the upcoming
Triathlon taking place on October 10, 2021, and reiterated the Housing Bills and invited people to
reach out to her as she is happy to share any information she has. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
thanked Sharon Cody, and confirmed that fostering a dog during COVID was a great experience.

City Council Minutes  11  July 13, 2021
 Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley thanked the City and the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for putting on a
firework show this year at the Lake. She also thanked Sharon Cody and Dedicated Animal Welfare
Group ~ DAWG for her tireless work, saving thousands of pets and raising thousands of dollars,
and thanked the Library for welcoming the public back and reinstating the Summer Reading
Program. Mayor Kelley mentioned that she attended the Mission Viejo Artisan Faire at the
Kaleidoscope Entertainment Center, and the upcoming Pacific Symphony event on August 14,
2021, at the Village Green. Lastly, she stated that kids will be going back to school mid-August
and that City staff have been working hard to keep the Recreation Centers up and running. Part of
the problem is a shortage of lifeguard staff, and she hopes the recreation swimming time can be
expanded at Montanoso as currently only lap swimmers can make a reservation. Mayor Kelley did
express kudos to staff for getting the facilities up and running again.
